We help leaders build across borders.

Book a callOur services

Who we are

Growing across borders usually means working with a lawyer, a mobility provider, a shipping company and a fit-out contractor, each with their own timelines. Artiq Global was built to replace that patchwork with one accountable team.

We advise on business setup and market entry, manage immigration and relocation for employees, and design and run workplaces. Because the services connect, a decision in one area does not surprise another.

Home / Blog / Relocation

Air or sea freight for your move?

Speed and cost pull in different directions, so many moves use both.

Book a callOur services

Air freight is faster and suits essentials you need on arrival. Sea freight takes longer and costs less per unit of volume, so it suits furniture and larger household goods.

Many moves combine both: a small air shipment for essentials and a sea shipment for the rest. Compare both for your route and dates before deciding.

Want help with this? Our team can walk you through the next steps for your situation.

Home / Blog / Business

What to decide before setting up a company abroad

Three early decisions shape every licence, filing and bank requirement that follows.

Book a callOur services

Before filing anything, settle three questions: where the business will operate from, who will own and manage it, and which activities it will carry out. These answers shape the entity type, licences and bank requirements, so changing them later is slow and costly.

Then list the approvals each activity needs, the documents your owners and directors must provide and the people you plan to hire in the first year. A short written plan saves weeks of back-and-forth with authorities and banks.

Want help with this? Our team can walk you through the next steps for your situation.

Home / Blog / Relocation

Domestic or international relocation: what changes

The same move gets more paperwork, more lead time and more choices abroad.

Book a callOur services

A domestic move is mostly about packing, transport and dates. An international move adds customs paperwork, shipping mode, insurance choices and often immigration requirements.

Plan an international move earlier, keep documents ready in one place and agree what goes by air, what goes by sea and what stays behind.

Want help with this? Our team can walk you through the next steps for your situation.

Home / Blog / Mobility

A simple timeline for an employee relocation

Start from the joining date and work backwards, with immigration first.

Book a callOur services

Start with the date the employee must begin work and count backwards. Immigration and visa steps usually set the earliest possible start, so they should be confirmed before shipping and housing are booked.

Then layer in housing, travel and household goods. Keeping one coordinator across all of these prevents gaps, such as a visa approved but no home ready.

Want help with this? Our team can walk you through the next steps for your situation.

Home / Blog / Mobility

Why visa planning should start early

Missing or inconsistent paperwork is a common cause of delay.

Book a callOur services

Visa timelines depend on the route, the applicant’s profile and the documents available. Missing or inconsistent paperwork is a common cause of delay.

Start by checking eligibility, collect documents early and confirm each form matches the others. Early planning also keeps your options open if requirements change.
